I'm designing a motion/"juice" system (animations, shader accents, interaction variants) for Twyne, a Qwik local-first writing app with an AI "room of editors" at /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne. Brand: editorial, letterpress, literary writer's room (paper, ink, stamps, vermilion/cobalt). I need a precise inventory of the **writers' room panels** — the editors (personas), their notes, the rubric/stamp, research — so every component can communicate what it is doing and what an interaction costs. Do not edit anything.

Scope:
- `src/components/editorial-board/editorial-board-overlay.tsx` + `board-tabs.ts`
- `src/components/personas/personas-panel.tsx` (big; grep) and other files in src/components/personas
- `src/components/rubric/*` including `stamp-shader.tsx` and the stamp press (`src/components/ui/stamp-press.tsx`, `workflow-stamp.tsx`) — global.css has `stamp-die-press`, `stamp-ink-settle`, `rubric-proof-settle`, `presswobble` keyframes (~lines 1799-2040)
- `src/components/comments/*`, `src/components/citations/*`
- `src/components/living-desk/*` (living-desk-panel, document-spine, living-desk.css) and `src/utils/living-desk/presence.ts`
- `src/components/instruments/*` (instrument-dock, instrument-room, task-desk, scene-bench, entity-instrument, instrument-art, instrument-motion — note instrument-motion.tsx already defines states rest/open/compare/arrive and a quiet flag)
- `src/components/ui/editorial-loader.tsx`, `application-notice.tsx`, `global-application-toasts.tsx`, `global-connectivity-banner.tsx`, `themed-dialog.tsx`, `text-modal.tsx`, `speak-button.tsx`, `global-speech-player.tsx`, `voice-recorder.tsx`, `live-voice-desk.tsx`
- `src/components/writing-tools/*` if not covered above.

For EACH component/sub-element report compactly:
1. file:line of root JSX and what it shows.
2. Interactions (hover, click, keyboard, drag) and what they do.
3. Current feedback/motion (class names, keyframes, global.css or component .css line numbers), including busy/thinking/waiting, error, success, empty variants. Specifically: how do we show that an editor (persona) is currently reading/thinking? How does a note "arrive"?
4. Consequence class: local-only, sends text to AI provider / spends hosted credits (and where cost or provider is shown), syncs, publishes, destructive.
5. Async lifecycles (queued → running → arrived → accepted/dismissed) and the store fields that represent them — these are hooks I can animate.

Also list the existing reusable motion pieces (keyframes, easing variables, reduced-motion handling, `quiet` mechanisms) so I can reuse rather than duplicate.

Return a structured, terse list with file:line references. Under ~1500 words.

- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.
